title: Lord’s Supper
definition: The Lord’s Supper is the ordinance in which believers remember and proclaim Christ’s death through the bread and the cup until He comes.
summary: The Lord’s Supper is the ordinance in which believers remember and proclaim Christ’s death through the bread and the cup until He comes.
christFocus: Jesus gave the Supper to His people as a Gospel sign of His body given and His blood poured out for sinners.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Lord’s Supper keeps the Church close to the cross. Through the bread and cup, believers remember that forgiveness, fellowship, and hope come through Christ’s sacrificed body and shed blood.

The Supper is not a casual ritual. Scripture calls believers to examine themselves, discern the body, and receive it with faith, gratitude, repentance, and unity. It is a holy reminder of grace.

The Supper also points forward. The Church proclaims the Lord’s death until He comes, remembering the cross while waiting for the feast of the kingdom.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Believers are forgetful and easily drift from the Gospel. The Lord’s Supper regularly brings the Church back to Christ crucified for sinners.

This ordinance also speaks to the unworthy-feeling believer. The table is not for people who saved themselves; it is for those who come to Christ in repentant faith and need His grace.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Come to the Lord’s Supper with reverence, repentance, and gratitude. Remember Christ’s sacrifice, seek reconciliation where needed, and let the Gospel renew your worship and unity with His people.
